in_arabic.name: سيدات
in_arabic.long_meaning: سيدات هو مصطلح عربي يُستخدم للنساء المرموقات والمتعلمات، وله جذور في اللغة العربية، ويشير إلى النساء ذوات المناصب الرفيعة والمرموقة في المجتمع الإسلامي، وله أهمية دينية وثقافية في التقليد الإسلامي

in_urdu.name: سیدات
in_urdu.meaning: عورتوں کے لیے ایک敬 اور محترم اصطلاح
in_urdu.long_meaning: سیدات ایک عربي اصطلاح ہے جو عورتوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے، جو敬 اور محترم ہوتی ہیں، اور اس کی جڑیں عربي زبان میں ہیں، اور یہ اصطلاح جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم روایت میں بھی استعمال ہوتی ہے

in_hindi.name: सैयदात

in_hindi.long_meaning: सैयदात एक अरबी शब्द है जो महिलाओं के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है, जो सम्मानित और शिक्षित होती हैं, और इसकी जड़ें अरबी भाषा में हैं, और यह शब्द भारतीय मुसलमान समुदाय में भी उपयोग किया जाता है

data.cultural_impact: The title "Sayyadat" holds a significant cultural impact, particularly in the Islamic world, representing a woman who serves as a traveler, guide, leader, teacher, or mentor to others. Historically, the term was often used to describe female Sufi saints and scholars who embarked upon spiritual journeys to enhance their knowledge and wisdom. In the context of Sufism, a mystical branch of Islam, the Sayyadat served as revered figures for their communities, embodying virtues of patience, wisdom, and selflessness.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the term "Sayyadat" rests in its connotation of spiritual guidance and enlightenment. The title signifies the role of a woman who has dedicated herself to the pursuit of knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth. Sayyidat represents a model of feminine strength, reverence, and resilience, encouraging self-reflection, introspection, and inner transformation. The title also symbolizes a deep connection to the Divine, inspiring devotion, humility, and a bond with the divine as a mentor or guide, reflecting the concept of Oneness between God and the human soul.
